canonical_name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
canonical_statement: For every nonzero natural modulus q and every unit residue class a in ZMod q, the set of natural primes whose residue modulo q equals a is infinite.
domain_and_universes: q : Nat; [NeZero q]; a : ZMod q; p : Nat
conclusion: {p : Nat | p.Prime and (p : ZMod q) = a}.Infinite

boundary_cases.q_one: included; ZMod 1 has its unit residue class and the target specializes to infinitude of all natural primes
boundary_cases.nonunit_residue: excluded by the explicit IsUnit a hypothesis

alternate_encodings.target: above every natural bound n there exists a prime p > n whose residue is a

minimal_import_evidence: The statement uses ZMod and its unit predicate from Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Coprime. The checked infinitude/unbounded transport uses Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt from Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Basic. Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.PrimesInAP, which contains the theorem proof, is deliberately not imported.

mutation_tests.mutation: replace natural primes by integers with prime natAbs
choose one modulus existentially instead of quantifying every modulus

foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory; the checked iff transport reports propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound; no custom axioms
computation_profile: No computation, oracle, experiment, or unchecked certificate is credited.
status_boundary: Exact statement and checked alternate transport only. The proof-bearing PrimesInAP module was not imported or credited; source audit, anchor audit, proof, validation, release, audit completion, and theorem completion remain open.
